Sanlam Share Price (JSE: SLM) Risks Breakdown Below R81 Support as Rand, Weather Claims Weigh on Earnings

Sanlam shares came under pressure after a sharp first-half profit decline, with weather-related claims, currency movements and weaker insurance margins raising caution despite stronger cash flows and solid returns.

Written by: Skerdian Meta • Thursday, September 10, 2026 • 3 min read
• Last updated: Friday, September 11, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:16
Instaread

Sanlam shares came under pressure after a sharp first-half profit decline, with weather-related claims, currency movements and weaker insurance margins raising caution despite stronger cash flows and solid returns.

Weather Claims Erase Underlying Growth

Sanlam said comparable core earnings increased only 1% during the six months ended June 30, 2026. Management estimates that sustainable underlying growth was closer to 7%, but weather-related and abnormal claims reduced earnings by approximately 8%.

Floods, wildfires and other large insurance losses created significant pressure, particularly across South Africa and broader Africa. Santam absorbed almost R700 million of flood and wildfire claims net of reinsurance.

The result highlights the difficulty insurers face when severe weather events occur during an otherwise constructive operating period. Although management expects weather losses to moderate in the second half, the first-half impact has already weakened the annual earnings picture.

Strong Cash Flows Provide Some Support

Despite the weaker profit result, Sanlam continued to generate strong client activity. Net client cash flows reached R78 billion, while total new business volumes increased 22% on a comparable basis.

Asset management was a particularly strong contributor, with core earnings increasing 48%. Life insurance also performed positively, generating just under R5 billion in core earnings.

Adjusted return on equity reached 18.4% annualized, above Sanlam’s five-year average of 17% and comfortably above its cost of capital.

These figures suggest the underlying franchise remains healthy, although performance is becoming increasingly uneven between business segments.

Sanlam Shares Fall as Profit Declines

Sanlam shares fell sharply following the insurer’s first-half results, with the JSE-listed SLM share price dropping 4.13% to around R81.70. The decline came after first-half profit fell 22%, as severe weather-related claims in South Africa and a stronger rand reduced the translated value of earnings generated outside the country.

The headline decline contrasts with several stronger underlying indicators. Sanlam reported healthy client activity, net client cash flows of R78 billion and a 22% increase in comparable new business volumes. However, investors appeared more concerned about slowing earnings growth and continued weakness in parts of the insurance operation.

Pan Africa Insurance Remains a Weak Point

General insurance remains one of Sanlam’s biggest concerns. Underwriting margins in Pan Africa remained below target, reflecting pressure from claims and operating conditions.

Malaysia is another area requiring attention, with elevated medical claims and regulatory pressures expected to continue affecting performance.

Management is therefore shifting its focus from expansion toward improving returns, cash conversion and capital allocation. The strategy includes addressing underperforming businesses and improving the product mix.

Strategic Restructuring Continues

Sanlam completed important strategic transactions involving Ninety One and reshaped its India portfolio during the period.

The group is also expanding its integrated financial-services strategy through its GoTyme banking partnership and the SanlamAllianz joint venture in Africa.

These initiatives could strengthen the group over the longer term, but investors will want evidence that the investments translate into higher returns rather than simply adding complexity and costs.

Dividend Outlook Remains Positive

Sanlam said it expects to meet its full-year 2026 dividend guidance, supported by strong cash generation and a solid solvency position.

The company has also maintained a long record of dividend payments, giving income-focused investors some reassurance despite the weaker first-half earnings.

However, maintaining distributions while managing claims volatility, strategic investments and weaker business units will require disciplined capital allocation.

Second Half Could Remain Uneven

Management expects weather-related losses to ease during the second half, which could provide some relief. However, the loss of the Bonitas Medical Fund contract is expected to have a greater impact later in the year, while Malaysia remains a turnaround challenge.

Sanlam is targeting adjusted ROE above 20% by 2030, but reaching that goal will depend on stronger execution across weaker operations.

For now, the return toward R81.70 leaves SLM shares under pressure. Strong client flows, new business growth and capital strength provide support, but the sharp profit decline, insurance claims and currency headwinds suggest investors may remain cautious until Sanlam demonstrates more consistent earnings growth.
